note: Three directions compare the same event entry and judging tasks. Illustrative sample data; no product changes.

prompts.prompt:
Create a high fidelity desktop UI design comparison board for HackJudge, a hackathon and technical competition project platform. Output a wide landscape board with two equally sized complete desktop app screenshots side by side, left EVENT ENTRY, right JUDGING. Screens must have readable UI, no browser/device chrome, no perspective, no photographic environment, no poster composition. Above both small direction title and "Concept only · Sample data". Same sample content in both: CivicHacks 2026, Hackathon, October 12, 12 projects. Shared navigation HackJudge, Events, Projects, Judging. Event entry has event heading, event-stage "Judging open", concise description, prominent "Start judging", project browse section with Voltify, AgriSense, MedSync, LinguaLink; summaries say what was built; screenshots are small illustrative sample app interfaces, NOT abstract geometric covers. Judge workspace has progress "4 of 12 reviewed", selected project Voltify with summary "Predict peak demand and shift energy use across community buildings.", Team Aurora, track Energy, evidence actions "View demo" and "Repository", scoring criteria Innovation, Impact, Execution with 1–5 selection controls, private notes, visible "Local draft" and "Save & next". No claimed server saves or awards. Keep judging readability high, restrained accents, familiar task controls, panels and useful clear information. This is Operate mode. Make it beautiful through precise typography, rhythm, density and content. Avoid biomedical greens, soft bubbly font, marketing hero, decorative abstract geometry, sci-fi effects, gradients and glowing UI. Same content across variants.
Direction title "01 / Submission workspace". Visual world derived from conference submission portals: bright white and cool light gray, charcoal type, deep cobalt restrained accent. Clear workhorse sans typography. Shared narrow top nav with solid blue active underline, event title at 32px, compact contextual subnav Overview / Projects / My judging. Left screenshot has spacious event context band, compact judging assignment callout with start action on right, below two-column project cards showing small functional prototype previews and substantive summaries, a narrow event facts column. Right screenshot uses 30% project context left and 70% rubric right, white panels, gray fine dividers, large accessible square score buttons. The overall composition feels thoughtfully designed and approachable, credible competition platform. Tiny format chips at bottom show Hackathon blue, Demo Day orange, Code & Tell purple with unchanged base identity.

Direction title "02 / Build review". Left screenshot has event overview header, judging assignment horizontal band and a substantial project explorer with searchable rows; selected project reveals prototype preview and descriptive text in adjacent inspector. Direction title "03 / Competition desk". Visual world derived from event schedules and gate boards translated into a real competition app, never literally boarding passes or travel imagery. Near-white white and dark ink, restrained burnt orange accent, navy horizontal top bar. Strong normal sans headings and aligned tabular counts, precise rectangular sections with slim separators, no mono uppercase microtext. Left screenshot has main event name and a compact status/actions strip, below a broad project table with columns Project / Track / Review status / Open, and a narrower Your judging section with 4 of 12 reviewed and Start judging; short descriptions visible below each project name. Right screenshot has a horizontal queue strip along top with numbered projects and progress, below a left project evidence panel and a wider white rubric panel, orange selected score and save action. Structure supports time-pressured competition work, no decorative trophies, leaderboard gamification or fake ranks. Elegant density balanced with generous breathing room around important actions.
